lines: Progressive fatigue, early satiety, and unintentional weight loss over the past three months

His past medical history is notable for hypertension but no known malignancy.

encounters.cc: Memory issues over the past year including misplacing items and difficulty remembering names of new acquaintances

lines: Memory issues over the past year including misplacing items and difficulty remembering names of new acquaintances
The patient returns for follow-up of cognitive symptoms one year following his primary myelofibrosis diagnosis and ongoing management of Paget disease and chronic bronchitis.
His care partner is concerned because he occasionally forgets where he places his keys and has trouble remembering the names of new acquaintances.
He also mentions difficulty finding the right words during conversations.
However, he remains active in his community, pays his bills on time, and has no trouble managing his medications.
His sleep pattern has changed slightly; he now wakes up earlier than he used to but does not feel fatigued during the day.
- Older brother: Paget disease of bone
Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2 years ago.
On examination, the patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time.
His Mini-Mental State Examination score is 28/30, losing points only for delayed recall.
Complete blood count: within normal limits
Vitamin B12 level: within normal limits

encounters.cc: Two-week history of right anterior thigh pain radiating to medial knee with difficulty climbing stairs and rising from chairs

lines: Two-week history of right anterior thigh pain radiating to medial knee with difficulty climbing stairs and rising from chairs
The patient, with established lumbar osteoarthritis with radiculopathy, returns to neurology six months after prior evaluation for memory concerns.
He describes a dull ache in the anterior thigh that occasionally radiates toward the medial knee.
The pain is aggravated by walking uphill and improves with rest.
He also reports that his right leg feels weaker, especially when trying to rise from a chair or step onto a curb.
He has no bowel or bladder incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or back trauma.
His medical history includes long-standing lumbar osteoarthritis and poorly controlled hypertension.
- Older brother: Paget disease of bone
Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2 years ago.
On physical examination, strength testing reveals 4/5 strength with right knee extension, while hip flexion and ankle movements are intact.
The right patellar reflex is diminished compared to the left.
Sensation to pinprick and light touch is reduced over the anterior thigh and medial shin.
Straight leg raise test is negative.
An MRI of the lumbar spine is ordered to evaluate suspected radiculopathy.

lines: Blood in urine noticed this morning, described as present at the beginning of urination but clearing by the end of the stream

He describes the blood as being present at the beginning of urination but clears by the end of the stream.
He denies any recent trauma or vigorous exercise.
His past medical history includes benign prostatic hyperplasia and hypertension,.
He takes which are managed with tamsulosin and lisinopril, respectively.

Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2 years ago.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and he is afebrile.
Abdominal examination is unremarkable with no flank tenderness.
Genitourinary examination reveals a mildly enlarged, non-tender prostate.
There is no meatal discharge or lesions.
- Urinalysis: Red blood cells present, no casts
- Complete blood count: Within normal limits

encounters.cc: Recurrent episodes of dizziness and one episode of syncope while shaving this morning preceded by light-headedness

lines: Recurrent episodes of dizziness and one episode of syncope while shaving this morning preceded by light-headedness
This patient with carotid sinus hypersensitivity returns with dizziness and syncope that occurred while he was shaving this morning.
He reports that the syncope was preceded by a sensation of light-headedness and "blacking out."
His past medical history is significant for hypertension.
- Older brother: Paget disease of bone
Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2 years ago.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 145/90 mm Hg, and his heart rate is 78 beats per minute.
Carotid sinus massage is performed in a controlled setting, which results in a 4-second pause in ventricular rate and a drop in systolic blood pressure to 85 mm Hg.

encounters.cc: Acute onset of agitation, confusion, severe headache, and flushed appearance 48 hours after admission for hypertensive emergency

lines: Acute onset of agitation, confusion, severe headache, and flushed appearance 48 hours after admission for hypertensive emergency
The patient is a 70-year-old male with hypertension, chronic kidney disease, mild neurocognitive disorder, and primary myelofibrosis who was admitted for hypertensive emergency.
He is started on an intravenous infusion of sodium nitroprusside.
After 48 hours of treatment, the nursing staff reports that the patient has become increasingly agitated and confused.
He complains of a severe headache and has become flushed.
His wife mentions that he seems to be breathing more heavily than usual.
- Older brother: Paget disease of bone
Smoking: Former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2 years ago.
On examination, his blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 102 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 94% on room air.
An arterial blood gas shows a pH of 7.35, PaCO2 of 45 mmHg, and PaO2 of 85 mmHg.
The ECG shows sinus tachycardia with no other abnormalities.
